current_english: and how Mordecai, of Jewish descent, was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and pleasing to the populace of his brothers, seeking good things for his people and speaking the things that pertained to the peace of his seed. And Mordecai said, "These things have been done by God. I remembered the dream that I had seen, which signified these same things, and not one of them was in vain. The little spring, which grew into a river, and was turned into light and the sun, and overflowed into abundant waters, is Esther, whom the king took as a wife and willed to be queen. Now the two dragons are I and Haman. The nations that had assembled are those who attempted to blot out the name of the Jews. But my nation is Israel, which cried out to the Lord, and the Lord saved His people; and He freed us from all evils and performed great signs and wonders among the nations; and He commanded that there be two lots, one for the people of God, and the other for all the nations. And each of the two lots came to the day already fixed from that time before God for all the nations, and the Lord remembered His people and showed mercy to His inheritance. And these days will be observed in the month of Adar on the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with all eagerness and joy, in one assembly of the gathered people, for all succeeding generations of the people of Israel."
proposed_english: and how Mordecai, of Jewish descent, was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and pleasing to the populace of his brothers, seeking good things for his people and speaking the things that pertained to the peace of his seed.
current_note: Mordecai's interpretation of his dream (deuterocanonical Addition F; Vulgate 10:4-13, so numbered in the Saints Latin Critical Text) is included here in 10:3, where the Greek Esther places it. Notable Vulgate-distinct readings include "commanded that there be two lots" (praecepit, Greek "made") and the dense clause "to the day already fixed from that time before God for all the nations" (in statutum ex illo jam tempore diem coram Deo universis gentibus, taking the prepositionless dative universis gentibus as "for all the nations," where the Greek reads "to the hour and time and day of judgment before God and among all the nations").
proposed_note: In native Clementine Vulgate versification, 10:3 concludes the canonical Hebrew-based narrative, while Mordecai's interpretation of his dream (Addition F) follows as 10:4-13 (mapped to Saints.Bible 10:3 in parallel display).

proposed_english: You know all things, and You know that it was not out of pride and insolence, or any desire for glory, that I did this, refusing to bow down before the most proud Haman

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 13:14.

proposed_english: And when she had laid aside her royal garments, she put on clothing suited for weeping and mourning; and instead of various perfumes, she filled her head with ashes and dung, and humbled her body with fastings; and all the places in which she had previously been accustomed to rejoice, she filled with the tearing of her hair.

source_phrase: Nos autem libera manu tua, et adjuva me, nullum aliud auxilium habentem nisi te, Domine, qui habes omnium scientiam,

source_phrase: Cumque regio fulgeret habitu, et invocasset omnium rectorem et salvatorem Deum, assumpsit duas famulas,

proposed_english: Having therefore entered all the doors in order, she stood opposite the king, where he sat upon the throne of his kingdom, clothed in royal garments and shining with gold and precious stones; and he was terrifying in appearance.

source_phrase: Quid habes, Esther? ego sum frater tuus: noli metuere.
proposed_english: "What is the matter with you, Esther? I am your brother; do not be afraid.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:12.

source_phrase: Non morieris: non enim pro te, sed pro omnibus hæc lex constituta est.
proposed_english: You will not die, for this law was established not for you, but for all.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:13.

source_phrase: Accede igitur, et tange sceptrum.
proposed_english: Come near therefore, and touch the scepter."
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:14.

source_phrase: Cumque illa reticeret, tulit auream virgam, et posuit super collum ejus, et osculatus est eam, et ait: Cur mihi non loqueris?
proposed_english: And when she remained silent, he took the golden scepter and placed it upon her neck, and kissed her, and said, "Why do you not speak to me?"
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:15.

source_phrase: Quæ respondit: Vidi te, domine, quasi angelum Dei, et conturbatum est cor meum præ timore gloriæ tuæ.

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:16.

source_phrase: Valde enim mirabilis es, domine, et facies tua plena est gratiarum.
proposed_english: For you are very wonderful, my lord, and your face is full of graces."
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:17.

source_phrase: Cumque loqueretur, rursus corruit, et pene exanimata est.
proposed_english: And while she was speaking, she collapsed again and nearly fainted away.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:18.

source_phrase: Rex autem turbabatur, et omnes ministri ejus consolabantur eam.
proposed_english: Now the king was distressed, and all his attendants were comforting her.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 15:19.

proposed_english: "The great King Artaxerxes, from India to Ethiopia, to the leaders and princes of the one hundred twenty-seven provinces who obey our command, sends greeting.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:1.

source_phrase: Multi bonitate principum et honore, qui in eos collatus est, abusi sunt in superbiam:

proposed_english: and not only do they strive to oppress those subject to kings, but not enduring the glory given to them, they plot ambushes against the very ones who gave it.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:3.

source_phrase: Nec contenti sunt gratias non agere beneficiis, et humanitatis in se jura violare, sed Dei quoque cuncta cernentis arbitrantur se posse fugere sententiam.
proposed_english: Nor are they content not to give thanks for kindnesses and to violate the laws of humanity within themselves, but they even suppose that they can escape the sentence of God, who sees all things.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:4.

source_phrase: Et in tantum vesaniæ proruperunt, ut eos qui credita sibi officia diligenter observant, et ita cuncta agunt ut omnium laude digni sint, mendaciorum cuniculis conentur subvertere,
proposed_english: And they have broken out into such madness that they attempt to undermine by tunnels of lies those who diligently keep the offices entrusted to them and conduct everything so as to be worthy of everyone's praise,

source_phrase: dum aures principum simplices, et ex sua natura alios æstimantes, callida fraude decipiunt.
proposed_english: while with clever deceit they deceive the simple ears of princes who judge others from their own nature.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:6.

source_phrase: Quæ res et ex veteribus probatur historiis, et ex his quæ geruntur quotidie, quomodo malis quorumdam suggestionibus regum studia depraventur.
proposed_english: And this matter is proved both from ancient histories and from the things that take place daily, how the aims of kings are corrupted by the evil suggestions of certain men.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:7.

source_phrase: Unde providendum est paci omnium provinciarum.
proposed_english: For this reason, provision must be made for the peace of all the provinces.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:8.

proposed_english: Nor ought you to think, if we give different commands, that this comes from the fickleness of our mind, but that we pass judgment according to the character and necessity of the times, as the welfare of the commonwealth demands.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:9.

source_phrase: Et ut manifestius quod dicimus intelligatis, Aman filius Amadathi, et animo et gente Macedo, alienusque a Persarum sanguine, et pietatem nostram sua crudelitate commaculans, peregrinus a nobis susceptus est:
proposed_english: And so that you may understand more clearly what we say: Haman the son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian in both spirit and nation, and alien to the blood of the Persians, and staining our goodness with his cruelty, was received by us as a foreigner,
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:10.

source_phrase: et tantam in se expertus humanitatem, ut pater noster vocaretur, et adoraretur ab omnibus post regem secundus:

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:11.

source_phrase: qui in tantum arrogantiæ tumorem sublatus est, ut regno privare nos niteretur et spiritu.
proposed_english: who was lifted up into such a swelling of arrogance that he strove to deprive us of both kingdom and breath.

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:13.

source_phrase: hoc cogitans ut illis interfectis, insidiaretur nostræ solitudini, et regnum Persarum transferret in Macedonas.
proposed_english: intending this: that once they were killed, he might lay an ambush against our isolation and transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:14.

source_phrase: Nos autem a pessimo mortalium Judæos neci destinatos, in nulla penitus culpa reperimus, sed e contrario justis utentes legibus,

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:15.

proposed_english: and sons of the Most High and greatest and ever-living God, by whose kindness the kingdom was handed down both to our fathers and to us, and is guarded to this very day.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:16.

source_phrase: Unde eas litteras, quas sub nomine nostro ille direxerat, sciatis esse irritas.
proposed_english: Therefore, know that those letters which he had sent out under our name are void.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:17.

source_phrase: Pro quo scelere ante portas hujus urbis, id est, Susan, et ipse qui machinatus est, et omnis cognatio ejus pendet in patibulis: non nobis, sed Deo reddente ei quod meruit.
proposed_english: For which crime, before the gates of this city, that is, Susa, both he himself who schemed it and all his kindred hang on gallows, with not us, but God repaying him what he deserved.

reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:18.

source_phrase: Hoc autem edictum, quod nunc mittimus, in cunctis urbibus proponatur, ut liceat Judæis uti legibus suis.
proposed_english: Now let this edict, which we are now sending, be posted in all the cities, so that it may be permitted for the Jews to follow their own laws.

proposed_english: To them you must be a support, so that they may be able to put to death those who had prepared themselves for their slaughter on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is called Adar.
reason: Stage 1 restored Clementine Vulgate Esther 16:20.

source_phrase: Hanc enim diem, Deus omnipotens, mœroris et luctus, eis vertit in gaudium.

proposed_english: Now let every province and city that refuses to share in this observance perish by sword and fire, and be so destroyed that it becomes impassable forever not only to humans, but even to beasts, as an example of contempt and disobedience."

source_phrase: Mens justi... (15:28) through Melius est parum cum justitia... (16:8)
current_english: The mind of the righteous meditates on obedience; the mouth of the wicked overflows with evil things. When the ways of a man please the Lord, He will turn even his enemies to peace.
proposed_english: The mind of the righteous meditates on obedience; the mouth of the wicked overflows with evil things.
current_note: The second sentence here is a Septuagint-derived addition in the Vulgate corresponding to Hebrew 16:6 (the Latin also gives that proverb at 16:6). The second sentences of 15:28 and 15:29 are numbered 16:7 and 16:8 in the Latin text and stand here following the Septuagint arrangement.
proposed_note: The second sentence of 15:27 is a Septuagint-derived addition in the Vulgate corresponding to 16:6. In native Vulgate order, 15:28 ('The mind of the righteous...') and 15:29 ('The Lord is far away...') stand separately from 16:1, 16:3, 16:4, 16:6, 16:7 ('When the ways of a man please the Lord, He will turn even his enemies to peace.'), 16:8 ('A little with righteousness is better than many fruits with unrighteousness.'), and restored 16:9, whereas Saints/Septuagint merges 16:7-8 into 15:28-29 and places 16:5b at 16:7.
reason: Rule 2 native-Vulgate order & Saints.Bible parallel mapping for Proverbs 15:27-29 and 16:1-9 (including formerly unplaced 16:1, 16:3, 16:6 and mapped 16:7-8).

source_phrase: Universa propter semetipsum operatus est Dominus; impium quoque ad diem malum.
current_english: The Lord has made everything for His own sake, even the wicked for the evil day.
proposed_english: The Lord has made everything for His own sake, even the wicked for the evil day.
current_note: Vulgate reads 'propter semetipsum' ('for His own sake'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly understood as 'for its own purpose.' This verse corresponds to 16:4 in the Hebrew text.

source_phrase: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Domini est dirigere gressus ejus.

reason: Stage 1 restored native Vulgate Proverbs 16:9 ('Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Domini est dirigere gressus ejus.') and returned Vulgate 16:4 to its native 16:4 slot.

source_phrase: Quis potest dicere: Mundum est cor meum; purus sum a peccato? | Qui maledicit patri suo et matri, extinguetur lucerna ejus in mediis tenebris: hæreditas ad quam festinatur in principio, in novissimo benedictione carebit. Ne dicas: Reddam malum: exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te.
current_english: Who is able to say, "My heart is clean; I am pure from sin"? The one who curses his father and mother, his lamp will be extinguished in the midst of darkness; an inheritance toward which one hurries at the beginning will lack a blessing in the end. Do not say, "I will pay back evil." Wait for the Lord, and He will rescue you.
proposed_english: Who is able to say, "My heart is clean; I am pure from sin"?
current_note: The second, third, and fourth sentences are numbered 20:20-22 in the Latin text (as in the Hebrew); they stand here following the Septuagint arrangement.
proposed_note: In native Vulgate order (matching the Hebrew), 20:9 holds only 'Who is able to say, "My heart is clean; I am pure from sin"?', while the three following proverbs stand at their native Vulgate slots 20:20, 20:21, and 20:22 (after 20:14-19); Saints.Bible parallel display maps 20:20-22 into Saints 20:9 following the Septuagint arrangement.
reason: Rule 2 native-Vulgate order & Saints.Bible parallel mapping for Proverbs 20:9 and 20:20-22 (plus native slots for formerly unplaced 20:14-19).

source_phrase: Quid necesse est homini... (7:1) through et quis cognovit solutionem verbi? (7:30)
current_english: Why is it necessary for a person to seek things greater than himself, since he does not know what is beneficial for him in his life, for the number of the days of his sojourn and the time that passes by like a shadow? Or who will be able to show him what will be after him under the sun?
proposed_english: Why is it necessary for a person to seek things greater than himself, since he does not know what is beneficial for him in his life, for the number of the days of his sojourn and the time that passes by like a shadow? Or who will be able to show him what will be after him under the sun?
current_note: The Vulgate opens with Quid necesse est homini majora se quaerere ("Why is it necessary for a person to seek things greater than himself"), expanding on the brief Hebrew question, and renders the days of vanity as peregrinationis suae ("of his sojourn").
proposed_note: Native Vulgate opens chapter 7 with 'Quid necesse est homini...' (7:1 = Saints/Hebrew 6:12), shifting native Vulgate 7:2-30 one verse ahead of Saints/Hebrew 7:1-29 (with native 7:30 also including the two opening questions of Hebrew 8:1).
reason: Rule 2 native-Vulgate order & Saints.Bible parallel mapping for Ecclesiastes 7:1-30 (30 exact-shifted verses).

source_phrase: Nescivi: anima mea conturbavit me, propter quadrigas Aminadab.
current_english: I did not know: my soul threw me into turmoil because of the chariots of Amminadab.
proposed_english: I did not know: my soul threw me into turmoil because of the chariots of Amminadab.

Verse 6:12 ends chapter 6 in the Clementine Vulgate (Hebrew 6:13 corresponds to Vulgate 7:1).

source_phrase: Quid videbis in Sulamite, nisi choros castrorum? Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis, filia principis! Juncturæ femorum tuorum sicut monilia quæ fabricata sunt manu artificis.

source_phrase: Res Spiritus oris nostri, christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris, cui diximus: In umbra tua vivemus in gentibus.
current_english: Resh: The breath of our mouth, the anointed Lord, was captured in our sins, to whom we said, "In Your shadow we will live among the nations."
proposed_english: Resh: The breath of our mouth, the anointed Lord, was captured in our sins, to whom we said, "In Your shadow we will live among the nations."
current_note: Latin christus Dominus ("the anointed Lord") sets the two nouns in apposition, as the Septuagint does (christos kyrios), where the Hebrew reads "the anointed of the Lord"; the Vulgate also reads oris nostri ("of our mouth") and in peccatis nostris ("in our sins") where the Hebrew has "of our nostrils" and "in their pits."
proposed_note: Latin christus Dominus ("the anointed Lord" or "the anointed lord") sets the two nouns in apposition, as the Septuagint does (christos kyrios), where the Hebrew reads "the anointed of the Lord"; the Vulgate also reads oris nostri ("of our mouth") and in peccatis nostris ("in our sins") where the Hebrew has "of our nostrils" and "in their pits." Editorial policy review: capitalization of "Lord" and "Your" reflects a Christological reading alongside the historical royal referent (the captured Judean king, lowercase "anointed lord" / "your").
reason: Disputed Messianic capitalization ('the anointed Lord ... Your' for 'christus Dominus ... tua') in Lamentations 4:20 flagged for human editor review without silently forcing a change.

source_phrase: Multorum nobis et magnorum per legem, et prophetas, aliosque qui secuti sunt illos, sapientia demonstrata est, in quibus oportet laudare Israël doctrinæ et sapientiæ causa, quia non solum ipsos loquentes necesse est esse peritos, sed etiam extraneos posse et dicentes et scribentes doctissimos fieri. Avus meus Jesus, postquam se amplius dedit ad diligentiam lectionis legis, et prophetarum, et aliorum librorum qui nobis a parentibus nostris traditi sunt, voluit et ipse scribere aliquid horum quæ ad doctrinam et sapientiam pertinent, ut desiderantes discere, et illorum periti facti, magis magisque attendant animo, et confirmentur ad legitimam vitam. Hortor itaque venire vos cum benevolentia, et attentiori studio lectionem facere, et veniam habere in illis, in quibus videmur, sequentes imaginem sapientiæ, deficere in verborum compositione. Nam deficiunt verba hebraica, quando fuerint translata ad alteram linguam: non autem solum hæc, sed et ipsa lex, et prophetæ, ceteraque aliorum librorum non parvam habent differentiam quando inter se dicuntur. Nam in octavo et trigesimo anno temporibus Ptolemæi Evergetis regis, postquam perveni in Ægyptum, et cum multum temporis ibi fuissem, inveni ibi libros relictos, non parvæ neque contemnendæ doctrinæ. Itaque bonum et necessarium putavi et ipse aliquam addere diligentiam et laborem interpretandi librum istum: et multa vigilia attuli doctrinam in spatio temporis, ad illa quæ ad finem ducunt, librum istum dare, et illis qui volunt animum intendere, et discere quemadmodum oporteat instituere mores, qui secundum legem Domini proposuerint vitam agere. Omnis sapientia a Domino Deo est: et cum illo fuit semper, et est ante ævum.
current_english: All wisdom is from the Lord God, and was with Him always, and is before eternity.
proposed_english: The wisdom of many and great things has been shown to us through the law and the prophets and others who followed them, in which it is fitting to praise Israel for the sake of instruction and wisdom, because not only must the speakers themselves be skilled, but even outsiders can become most learned both by speaking and by writing. My grandfather Jesus, after he gave himself more fully to the diligent reading of the law and the prophets and the other books that were handed down to us by our forefathers, wished himself also to write something of these things that pertain to instruction and wisdom, so that those who desire to learn, having become skilled in them, may pay closer and closer attention in mind and be strengthened for a lawful life. Therefore I urge you to come with goodwill, and to read with more attentive zeal, and to grant indulgence in those places where we seem, while following the image of wisdom, to fall short in the phrasing of words. For Hebrew words fall short when they are translated into another language; and not only these, but even the law itself, and the prophets, and the rest of the other books have no small difference when they are spoken in themselves. For in the thirty-eighth year, in the times of King Ptolemy Euergetes, after I arrived in Egypt and had been there a long time, I found books left there of no small and no contemptible instruction. Therefore I thought it good and necessary for me myself also to add some diligence and labor in translating this book; and with much watchfulness I brought instruction over a span of time, to give this book for those things that lead to the end, and to those who wish to apply their mind and to learn how one ought to order conduct, who have resolved to live life according to the law of the Lord. All wisdom is from the Lord God, and was with Him always, and is before eternity.
current_note: Vulgate "ante ævum" ("before eternity" or "before the age") is a distinct Latin reading where the Greek has "forever" ("eis ton aiōna"), and the Vulgate also adds "God" ("Deo") after "the Lord."
